page.layout: One printed page (left page of a spread, the right page is cut off at the edge and only partly visible). Top: running head left "De rebus sacris." and page number 330 with "Lib.8." at top centre. Main text in one column. A brace on the left of the column groups four lines of text with the label "Primae sunt" and marginal references "ver.3.4."; the brace is a diagram-like grouping. Right edge: fragments of another page's text (not transcribed as it belongs to the neighbouring page).

main_text.p: Primae sunt ver.3.4.Mandatum quo iubebat eam educi extra castra vt iugulet quis eam ver. 3. Significabat autem Christum e terrestribus rebus acceptum & extra portam crucifixum fuisse. Heb. 13. 12. Aspersio sanguinis.
Aspersio sanguinis erat, qua ex eo, digito acceptum aspergebat, versus anteriorem partem tentorij conuentus, septies.
Actionem Christi quotidie per spiritum ecclesiam sanguine suo spargentem, ad perfectam iustificationis purgationem, significabat. Psal. 51. 5. 9. 1.Pet.1.2. inter se cum ceremonia collatis.
Prima, qua ante oculos suos pellem, cornua & sanguinem cum fimo eius iubebat.
Significabat Christum libenter, & voluntate sancta, se etiam crucis morti subijcisse, & separatum, in manus aduentantis tradidisse. Esa.53.13. Phil.2.8. Ioa.18.6.7.8. inter se collatis
Secunda, qua sacerdos assumens lignum cedrinum, & muscum, & dibaphum coccineum, proijcit ea intra rogum illius Iunicis. ver.6.26.

Significabat Christum vt vt respectu nostrorum peccatorum diuina maledictione combustum: per spiritum tamen se ἀμωμον, donis spiritus plenum Deo sacrificium ἐυωδίας obtulisse, ad nos purgandum aptissimum. Psal.51.9. Eph.4.2.

page.notes: The brace grouping the four lines at the top left is a bracketed outline of the verse references; the Greek words (ἀμωμον, ἐυωδίας) are transcribed as printed, possibly with printing errors. Right page is largely cut off and not transcribed.
